key_insight: The paper shows that combining data storytelling with interpretable machine learning can make AI decisions easier for non-experts to understand without exposing sensitive data.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical explanation layer for AI systems in high-stakes engineering and analytics workflows where transparency, usability, and data privacy must all be balanced.
method: Defined data storytelling for IML and proposed the DIST Pyramid to align storytelling with explainability goals.
Introduced an I-P-O model plus an architecture that generates "What-if" and "Why-not" explanations.
Used data desensitization and SHAP-driven, LLM-generated ABT stories in a Boston Housing case study.
evidence_signal: In the evaluation, 76.4% and 74.3% of respondents found the "What-if" and "Why-not" stories more comprehensible, with significantly higher accessibility scores than standard SHAP visualizations.
watch_item: Because the method relies on LLM-generated narratives and preprocessing for desensitization, explanation fidelity and privacy protection need careful validation across datasets and deployment settings.
paper_title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details
